title: Audit crashes and bugs
firstUserMessage:
Do another in-depth deep audit of the entire codebase and check if there are any unwired code or dependencies or app crashes [ app crashes prevention are important] or bugs - evaluate and resolve them. ALso look for possible incomplete codes, logics, and ways to improve / strengthen existing - evaluate them deeply and only implement the highest confidence and priority ones. review the recent code changes and the older code deeply and check for errors, crashes or new bugs. 

Post the above, share an end to end manual testing plan for the features in this chat. think deeply and use highest level of reasoning. be very detailed and in depth and evaluate the code with the highest possible technical lens for bugs, etc - code quality can be skipped, we will improve that later. looking for funtiomnal bugs, crashes, suspicious screens - for parts that are sus and might require a round of manual review - call them out and mention in the end to end testing plan so i can verify those too. Post this we will proceed to phase 11.

messages.text: I’ll do this as a crash-focused audit first: map the app, inspect recent diffs, run the available checks, then patch only the issues that look both high-confidence and high-impact. After that I’ll give you a manual test plan that includes the suspicious paths I’d want human eyes on before Phase 11.

messages.text: I’ve confirmed this is an iOS SwiftUI app with a dirty worktree already containing Phase 10-ish history/session changes. I’m going to treat those as user/recent changes, read around them carefully, and avoid broad refactors while looking for crash paths.

In parallel, I’ll read the main app wiring and the recent history/session changes that are most likely to affect launch, save, and planned-session completion.

messages.text: The first test run is still in Xcode’s simulator selection/build phase. While it runs, I’m scanning the code for the crash signatures that won’t always show up in unit tests: force unwraps, array indexing, async camera callbacks, persistence decoding, and navigation/session callback mismatches.

messages.text: The workspace run hit a locked Xcode build database, probably from the failed project build finishing too close to the workspace build. I’ll clear only DerivedData for this app and rerun the workspace test so we get a clean signal.

messages.text: I’m going to make a small crash-hardening patch now: protect the legacy `WorkoutPlan` bridge from empty exercise arrays, make readiness/motivation phrase selection impossible to index into an empty pool, and let older/corrupt-ish history entries recover `createdAt` from `endedAt` instead of dropping the whole history file. These are narrow, functional safety fixes rather than style work.
